message.reasoning: We need to answer: does enabling SSO immediately block staff not yet provisioned? According to policy: Enabling SSO does not immediately disable password sign-in for existing staff. Both methods coexist until admin turns password sign-in off. So flipping on SSO will not block staff; they can still use password sign-in until admin disables it. So answer: no, it won't block them. Provide explanation.

function.arguments: {"message":"Enabling SSO won’t lock staff out right away. When you turn on SSO, existing users can still sign in with their passwords. Password‑based sign‑in stays available until an admin explicitly disables it in Settings → Security → SSO → Require SSO. So you can enable SSO now and still let unprovisioned staff use their passwords until you’re ready to enforce SSO for everyone."}

arguments.message: Enabling SSO won’t lock staff out right away. When you turn on SSO, existing users can still sign in with their passwords. Password‑based sign‑in stays available until an admin explicitly disables it in Settings → Security → SSO → Require SSO. So you can enable SSO now and still let unprovisioned staff use their passwords until you’re ready to enforce SSO for everyone.
